## Barnabas (half-orc)

Barnabas was a half-orc thief in the Savage Frontier who worked as an agent of the ruler of Loudwater in the mid–14 century DR.

Personality
Barnabas was a highly intelligent individual and had an innate knack for acting.

Possessions
He typically dressed in a suit of leather armor and wielded a +1 dagger.

Relationships
Barnabas was a long-time friend of Nanathlor Greysword.

History
When Nanathlor Greysword first became the ruler of Loudwater in the, he hired Barnabas to work for him. Time and time again, he proved his worth in the tasks assigned to him. When the town became aware of the balor Grintharke and the wider machinations of the evil forces of Hellgate Keep, Barnabas suggested he become a spy and infiltrate their forces. Over time, Barnabas worked his way up the ranks.The original text stated that Barnabas's suggestion of infiltration came about "when Grintharke moved into Hellgate Keep", however, as later revealed in the adventure Hellgate Keep (pp. 4–5), Grintharke had been there since around 880 DR. Therefore it stands to reason that Barnabas's suggestion would have had to occur at some nebulous time when Loudwater became more aware of the dangers that Hellgate Keep posed.

Around the, the lich Pomerian led an army on behalf of Grintharke through the Underdark and back out to the surface in a surprise attack on the town of Llorkh. His forces comprised a horde of various orc tribes, a quarter of which were worg cavalry, 18 ogres from the Greypeak Mountains, 13 hill giants likewise from the Greypeaks, and 19 elite drow troops from Menzoberranzan. And amongst them was Barnabas, serving as one of Pomerian's minor staff officers.

Shortly before leading his army to the surface, Pomerian uncovered that Barnabas was a spy. Rather than eliminating him right away, the lich decided to keep the half-orc around and fed with nominal intel, reasoning that the double-agent could be exploited in the future to create diversions when needed. Using the Pipes of Doom, a bagpipes artifact that Grintharke's former master had created, the lich was able to rout Llorkh's forces before they had a chance to repulse the invasion. The Hellgate army then set their sights on the town of Loudwater, whose ruler was nevertheless able to prepare for an attack thanks to forewarning by Barnabas.

When the Battle of Loudwater commenced, Pomerian darkened the fair skies by summoning thick, foreboding clouds with the Pipes of Doom's control weather power. He then used spell scrolls to cast mass invisibility on his drow forces, enabling them to attempt a stealth attack on the enemy command post. Finally, the lich took to the center of the horde, flanked by ogres, and proceeded to play the Pipes of Doom to induce a steady retreat from the forces amassed at Loudwater.

Which side was victorious in this battle was ultimately uncertain, though the odds were firmly stacked against the forces of Loudwater and they were said to have suffered staggering losses. With a draw in the conflict, the Hellgate army set up camp for the night near the South Wood, working to construct huge rafts with which to cross the otherwise impassable River Shining.

Shortly after the night's evenfeast, while Pomerian plotted the next day's strategy within his command tent, a group of korreds snuck into camp and stole the Pipes of Doom. Once Pomerian realized they were missing, he sent a force of elite individuals out into the woods to recover the stolen Pipes and kill the thieving korreds. Lead by the fire giant Slag, they included the drow Lilliana, George the gorgon, and roguish twin princes Dammek and Dammon.

Barnabas took this opportunity to slink off to the opposing camp and tell Nanathlor what had transpired and of Pomerian's arrogance. He did not know what the creatures were that had stolen the Pipes of Doom, describing them as being the size of gnomes, but with long wild hair and beards, overall hairy bodies that smelled of fresh dirt and pine needles, and legs like a satyr. He spoke of the leader of these creatures having used a large pair of silver shears to slice through the canvas of Pomerian's tent and leaving without attacking anyone, save for some guards they had tossed into the woods. Before he could go on, Barnabas was interrupted by Traskar Selarn, ruler of the allied town of Secomber, who proclaimed that his description sounded like korreds and opined that they must be immune to the effects of the Pipes of Doom. With slow deliberation, Nanathlor agreed. This gave the forces of Loudwater newfound hope, for if they could retrieve the Pipes before the Hellgate army and destroy them, Loudwater would have a chance at routing the invaders. And so, after receiving further intel from Barnabas on the forces sent to retrieve the bagpipes, a group of renowned adventurers set forth on this quest.

Unfortunately for Barnabas, when he returned to the Hellgate camp he was swiftly detained under suspicion. Pomerian subjected him to an ESP spell, probing his mind for what had just went down back at Nanathalor's camp. Then, seeing no further use for the spy, Pomerian killed Barnabas and left to join his dispatched squad in the recovery of the Pipes of Doom.

## Battle of the Under Way

The Battle of the Under Way, also known as Comragh na Uamh in Dwarvish, was a battle that took place in the Under Way of Gauntlgrym between the dwarves of Mithral Hall and the forces of the drow House Xorlarrin in the, during the reclamation of Gauntlgrym.

History
During the reclamation of Gauntlgrym, Connerad Brawnanvil, with Bungalow Thump at his side, led the dwarven forces to the Under Way. Their army was aided by five young mages of the famous Harpell family, among them Kenneally, Tuckernuck, and Toliver Harpell.

While exploring the upper complex, they found each of their patrols returning to the same central corridor, and the only way down to the deeper levels was by a hole in the roof of a vast cavern. A thick door in the floor closed this hole, and led to a landing suspended on the cavern ceiling. The sheer drop proved a challenge for the dwarven forces, but by utilizing a magical Field of Feather Falling invented by Tuckernuck Harpell, the dwarven battleragers dropped to the bottom in groups of ten, with the spell catching them in the air and letting them float the last  or so to the ground. Both Connerad and Bungalow were among the first group, despite the unknown risk of enemies below.

After more than a hundred dwarves had successfully floated to the floor below, however, they were ambushed by the drow forces led by two wizard commanders, Jaemas and Faelas Xorlarrin. They had had an army of slaves, consisting mostly of goblins, orcs, and kobolds hidden in concealed tunnels disguised behind stone slabs.

Knowing that the large host of dwarven battleragers outmatched their own slave forces, and having watched in secret and observed the Harpells installing the Field of Feather Falling, the two drow mages focused on dismantling the enchantment. They cast magical bolts of lightning at the Harpells, striking Toliver and disabling the Feather Fall, so the next three groups of incoming dwarves, thirty in all, fell to their deaths. Frantically, the flying Harpell mages created a new Field of Feather Falling further along the landing, but it was too high, so the dwarves floated the whole way down, delaying their arrival and making them easy targets.

To the horror of the suddenly outnumbered dwarves at the bottom, a small host of demons then joined the drow army. These included flying chasme and they were led by a four-armed glabrezu demon.

With the mages' fireballs exploding around them, setting both goblins and one unlucky dwarf aflame, Connerad Brawnanvil took on the demons, but was soon torn in two by the glabrezu.

## Baldur's Bones

Baldur's Bones was a dice game popular in many taverns across the city of Baldur's Gate in the late 15 century DR, including the likes of the Elfsong Tavern and Low Lantern.

Rules
At the beginning of a game of Baldur's Bones, each player would put an agreed-upon ante into a pot. Each player needed three six-sided dice in order to play. After everyone paid their wagers, players would roll their starting dice and then play would proceed clockwise, with the host of the game intended to always go last.

On a given turn, a player could choose to roll or "stand", meaning they passed their turn over to the next player. If a player chose to "roll", they were given an additional die to roll. Once the roll was made, the player would once again be presented with the two options of "stand" or "roll" until they made the decision to end their turn.

The objective of the game was to have the highest numerical total on one's collective dice, with the highest numerical value allowed being 21. If a "roll" resulted in a collective value higher than 21, the player was considered to have "bust" and be out of the game. The player with the highest total at the end of play would win the ante pot.

Notable Baldur's Bones Players
 Brinks
 Bruno Indomicus
 Tarina, a former pirate who retired to the city of Baldur's Gate, was an avid player of the game and frequent cheater, playing games at the Elfsong Tavern.

## Battle of Ejen Horo

The Battle of Ejen Horo was a battle that occurred in the Hordelands in 1335 DR, in the valley of Ejen Horo, between a group of Tuigan warriors of the Hoekun clan and a company of ogres.

Location
This battle was fought on the west side of a fairly substantial, though shallow, creek that ran through a gully in Ejen Horo. This was close to the forested foothills beneath the Spiderhaunt Peaks.

History
This skirmish broke out over the killing and devouring the bodies of Yamun Khan's personal herd of Steppe horses by the coombe giant Billidûm and his band of Semphari ogres, having broken through their corral around night's end. Billidûm was vary wary in the lead up to the confrontation, warily standing watch for any sign of the Tuigans, much to the annoyance of the ogres. As dawn approached, the sun rising from the east, he sighted Yamun Khan riding from the west with a group of other warriors on horseback. Billidûm slammed his club against the ground and pointed in their direction, drawing the attention of the ogres, proclaiming, "We too long wait. Light come. And so do horse people. Come!"

The coombe giant's initial response was to flee to the safety of the nearby wooded foothils, the ogres following along in a ragged line. While tempted to give in to his blood lust, Billidûm recognized that their chances against the Hoekun in the open plains of Ejen Horo. He kept goading his men on, urging them to run faster from the quickly gaining horsemen, but their retreat was ultimately obstructed by a creek. As they got to the creek, from the near side came a line of light cavalrymen. Billidûm slit to a halt, thinking of what to do, whilst his ogres made exclamations and some began to chant their battle oaths.

Combatants

The sides were unevenly matched in terms of number of units. Billidûm's forces included twelve heavily armored ogres. Their weaponry included the likes of axes, maces, crude spears, swords, and warpicks. If necessary, they resorted to throwing rocks at the enemy. Billidûm himself wielded a massive tree trunk as an impromptu club.

Yamun Khan's forces included twelve light cavalrymen and six of his seven Valiant Men, all heavy cavalrymen astride on barded Steppe horses, something that was unusual for them to do with their steeds. The Khan's seventh man, General Chanar, was away on a mission at the time.

The twelve light cavalrymen were adorned in kalats, fur caps with long ear flaps, and hip bound quivers. The heavy cavalry were outfitted in black khalats and scale mail. The light cavalry wielded composite bows and lances, whilst the six heavy cavalrymen used composite bows, kama-yari, and curved swords.The weapons outlined in this article are approximated based on a combination of their appearance and Tuigan armament details from Horde Campaign, a book released in the same year that was designed to make use of the Battlesystem Miniatures Rules and miniatures such as these.

## Barausk

Barausk was a type of tree that grew in Harrowdale and Deepingdale in the Dalelands.

Description
It looked very similar to the beech tree and had black branches and a white trunk, and was covered in thorns  in length.

The wood of the barausk tree had a dark brown hue with gray-green mottling. On closer inspection, these gray-green areas marked where the grain folded back on itself to a very tight degree. Overall, the grain resembled a maze, meatballs amongst messed-up spaghetti, or the crazed banding that occurred around burls in other woods.

Usage

As the dense, folded grain dulled or even broke saws and blades, it could only be easily cut when green and wet, or after being soaked in water for around a day to soften. While it could be sprayed with water over a few days to achieve the same softening and enanle cutting, this was only to a depth of a finger's width, beyond which it must be sprayed again for continued cutting. Once the green wood was properly dried, barausk was as hard as iron and quite durable, but if heated it became brittle and could not be recovered. It took only 24 hours for the wood to dry until iron-hard.

Its wood was therefore used by many in woodworking projects. In particular, barausk wood, especially the branches, made for high-quality arrow shafts, spears, staves, and weapon hafts, and hence it was favored by hunters and soldiers. It was also used in alchemy for the extraction of silver vitriol and yellow vitriol, and in artificing and the crafting of a variety of implements for wizards, warlocks, and clerics.

## Bahrn

Bahrn was a mercenary of Turmish in the late 14 century DR.

Description
He had been a fat kid, with crooked teeth.

Personality
He was described as somewhat naive.

Abilities
He had an uncanny ability to use a morningstar by throwing it, being able to catch and pin someone's robe against a wall; this suggested he had absolutely incredible strength.

Possessions
He carried a morningstar, and wore a suit of fancy armor decorated with eye patterns made out of lapis lazuli.

Activities
He was a mercenary.

Relationships
His father was a farmer called Norint.

History
While a child, Bahrn and his friends had harassed Diadree, a local old woman living alone near Orunn, for which he'd gotten a broomstick shattered over his head, at some point after . He had left his home town of Orunn after his father died, when he was thirteen, becoming a mercenary afterwards. He was aware that it had been abandoned after it suddenly became geologically unstable in, with the earth becoming suddenly prone to frequent earthquakes which had rendered the land near-uninhabitable, almost certainly implying the events were chronologically close, if not related.

In the, he was hired by the wizard Arlon in Ironfang Deep as an escort and guide to Orunn; the wizard claimed that Diadree was his cousin, and a wizard to boot. Despite knowing that was fake, Bahrn agreed anyway, hoping to be there to prevent any harm that might befall her from Arlon; she was not known to have any friends. Indeed, once they neared her home, Bahrn failed to protect Arlon, whose face was roughed up by the old woman before he even noticed she was there. Bahrn convinced Arlon to be patient, rather than burn down her home, after she ran inside to hole up.

When she came back out, Bahrn caught her, and calmed her down somewhat; Arlon cast a spell on her clothes, which guided him to a ledge and cave.  Prompted by Diadree, who warned he was almost certainly a member of the Cult of the Dragon, Bahrn followed him, carrying Diadree to the cave. There, Arlon attacked Diadree, demanding to know where the dragon's body was; Bahrn protected Diadree, and hurled his morningstar at the man, pinning one of the arms of his robe to the wall with it somehow. That was enough for the cave's guardians to slay him.

He offered to carry Diadree out, but she refused; he said he'd at least fix her roof.

## Battle devourer

Battle devourers were former intellect devourers that had been modified for more military purposes. They were considered virtually unkillable.

Description
While similar in shape to their psionic cousins, battle devourers possessed green brains and bodies covered in jagged, stone-like armor plating. Their claws were sharper and more blade-like than those of normal intellect devourers.

Behavior
These aberrations were mostly aggressive on sight towards other creatures. They were always chaotic evil.

Abilities
These former intellect devourers no longer retained their psionic abilities. Battle devourers were completely immune to acid, cold, fire, and sonic damage, and they possessed minor resistance to electricity. They could withstand punishment even from the most powerful foes, unless struck by a weapon with a +3 enchantment or higher.

Battle devourers were both dexterous and resilient, noted for their heightened alertness, darkvision, and keen senses of sight and hearing. They could use their fear gaze up to six times per day. It worked similar to the fear spell. This ability affected all creatures within an area that did not resist its effect, thus becoming frightened.

In melee, their claw attacks not only dealt significant damage but could also slow enemies upon a successful hit.

Battle devourers were also able to spy on others and relay messages.

Usage
These aberrations were used as spies and messengers in the Underdark.

History
Sometime before Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, these creatures were bred for use as spies and messengers in the Underdark.

Around the 1370s DR, one could occasionally encounter these beings on the Sword Coast North, for example in the service of certain members of the Arcane Brotherhood within their Host Tower.

Ecology
Battle devourers could either be found alone or in small to medium groups. They were almost always aggressive on sight.

## Badger Bates

Badger Bates was a dwarf laborer in Sembia during the 13 and 14 centuries DR, who'd seen Malaeragoth during his razing of Uvalkhur's manor, avenging the wizard against his rivals; he was quite obsessive about that.

Personality
He talked a lot about that time he saw the sapphire dragon, Malaeragoth, razing Uvalkhur's manor to avenge the wizard against his rivals, making a big deal about the scale he'd picked up in the aftermath.

He was also very stingy with his money, unlike with the tale of his witnessing Malaeragoth, the steed of the wizard Uvalkhur, who razed the wizard's home after he was slain by rivals, slaying them one by one in his fury.

Activities
Badger Bates worked at a local foundry, though that was nothing compared to the fury of Malaeragoth, who slew all of Uvalkhur's rivals at his home after they finally killed the wizard, an act he'd witnessed at a previous job where he dug fountains for gardens.

Possessions
He owned a scale that had once belonged to the sapphire dragon Malaeragoth, whom he had witnessed in its rage, avenging the wizard Uvalkhur against the rivals that converged on his home to slay him.

Relationships
Badger Bates had a rivalry with the gnome Silvenestri Silver, both of them trying to one-up the other in dragon knowledge. He often brought up that he'd been the only person to witness Malaeragoth in his rage, for he'd been working on Uvalkhur's gardens when the wizard's rivals slew him, only to be struck down themselves by a raging Malaeragoth.

History

In the mid-to-late or late 13 century, Badger Bates had been digging a fountain for the wizard Uvalkhur's garden. While he worked, rivals attacked Uvalkhur's home and slew him; then the dragon Malaeragoth came, tore open the home, and slew one by one those rivals, an act which had only one surviving witness: Badger Bates himself. He managed to scrounge a single scale from the wreckage.

In the mid-winter of the, the Dragon Defeated sign got repainted; the owner, Varney, had it redrawn to resemble Badger and two other regulars: Silvenestri Silver and Wyrmbait Nix. They soon became local celebrities, "dragon experts", taking part of a contest every mid-tenday where they judged tales of dragons.

During the last such contest held, in late winter or early spring of that year,  the painter of the sign, Petra, challenged the judges' knowledge of dragons, and showed her own scrolls full of life drawings of actual dragons. Badger Bates dissmissed her paintings for not containing any pictures of Malaeragoth; when she claimed to have seen Malaeragoth more recently than he did, Bates demanded proof. She painted Malaeragoth on a wall of the tavern, but refused to draw his eyes, instead simply describing them. Bates refused to pay up unless the eyes were drawn.

The dwarf ultimately agreed to pay up once she drew the eyes. As she left, Badger insulted Malaeragoth; the picture came to life, destroyed the tavern, and slew him.

Rumors
There was a running bet that Badger Bates would not actually yield his scale to anyone, no matter what, at The Dragon Defeated.

## Backroad

A backroad, also known as a hidden path, was a mystical pathway of geomagical energy that connected two distant locations within the Prime Material plane. An uncountable number of backroads crisscrossed Faerûn, and entering a backroad allowed one to instantly traverse the full length of its path.

Description
Backroads did not correspond to any physical or observable roads, and could not be seen, felt, or tracked by nonmagical means. Only fey truly understood the backroads, allowing them to enter and navigate them more freely than nonfey. While travel along the backroads bore some resemblance to extraplanar travel, the backroads were actually a natural feature of the Prime Material plane.

Nonfey could only enter the backroads by a fey crossroads, and could only follow a single backroad to its predetermined destination (meaning they served nonfey more as portals than as roadways). Nonfey best understood the backroads as folds or pinches within the Prime Material plane that brought two distant points into close proximity.

Finding the entrance to a backroad could only be reliable done with a spell such as detect crossroads. A backroad could be created with the spell create crossroads and backroad, which was believed to be known only to some fey and druids.

History
Fey were the longtime guardians of the backroads, although they believed that they belonged to no one. In ancient times, the first elves were said to make use of the backroads.

When the drow of Maerimydra established their Land Under Shadow in  (in the area that would come to be known as Shadowdale), they were vexed by the high concentration of fey crossings and backroads in the area. They thus released a terrible monster called the Susurrus into the backroads, forcing the local fey to abandon them.

Because so few nonfey knew of the backroads or how they worked, many considered them to be merely legends. Faerûnian druids referred to the backroads as the "Hidden Paths", and had made efforts to map them. As of the mid-to-late 14 century DR, they had only discovered a relatively small number of them, and fey refused to share the secrets of the backroads with them or anyone else as they feared the possibility of the pathways becoming corrupted. A common use of the backroads among these druids was for communication as sound could freely travel the full length of a backroad between two fey crossroads.

The Selûnite Swords of the Lady were believed to have access to a number of backroads, which allowed them to move swiftly across the land to strike at their Sharran enemies.

## Battle of Freeman's Down

The Battle of Freeman's Down was a clash of the Northmen of Norland versus the Ffolk of eastern Corwell and their allies during the Darkwalker War of the . It occurred at Freeman's Down in the Highlands of Gwynneth as the Ffolk intercepted the Northmen while they attempted to march across the mountains.

Location
Freeman's Down was a small river valley in the mountains above the Corwell Road in central Corwell. It lay along the path of a low pass between the southern Myrloch Vale and Corwell. It was characterized by an open field bisected east-to-west by a narrow drainage ditch, and was bounded to the east by the Deep Stream and to the west by a low hill.

The site was selected by Prince Tristan Kendrick of Corwell for its geography, which he judged to be suitable for a defensive stand against the approaching Northmen army as it marched over the mountains from Myrloch Vale.

History
Causes
After razing the eastern cantrevs of Corwell throughout the month of Kythorn, King Grunnarch the Red of Norland and King Raag Hammerstaad of Norheim split their forces in order to surround and massacre the surviving Ffolk, who were fleeing west along Corwell Road, in accordance with a plan laid out by King Khelgar Ironfist. While Raag's forces marched along the Corwell Road with the bulk of the armies' supplies, Grunnarch marched his men over Dynloch Pass with the intention of cutting through Myrloch Vale to intercept the refugees, trapping them between the two armies. In truth, the plan was not devised by the true Khelgar Ironfist but by the Beast Kazgaroth, who used his vile magic to bolster Grunnarch's forces. This included transforming Grunnarch's Bloodriders, led by Laric, into blood warriors, and by corrupting the druid Trahern to serve as a guide through the Vale and to rendezvous the Northmen army with a force of firbolgs led by Groth.

Meanwhile, Prince Tristan Kendrick and his companions discovered the carnage in eastern Corwell on Kythorn 26, and resolved to pursue the Northmen through the mountains. Their band was joined by the Sisters of Synnoria on Kythorn 30, who pledged their allegiance to Tristan according to tradition when the mighty horse Avalon permitted the prince to ride him, and the Sisters took them via a shortcut through Synnoria to get ahead of Grunnarch's army. On Flamerule 3, they were joined by a force of dwarves led by Finellen, whom the band had previously rescued from firbolg imprisonment. The small force arrived at Freeman's Down ahead of the Northmen, who meanwhile were being harried and attacked by the forces of nature as directed by the Great Druid Genna Moonsinger. Tristan resolved to make a stand there in order to slow the enemy long enough for the Ffolk refugees to pass and escape the Northmen's trap. As his allies prepared the battleground, Tristan rode down to the Corwell Road in hopes of gathering a militia to fight alongside them. Despite his inexperience as a leader, he was surprisingly successful at rallying his people, and gathered six hundred able-bodied men and women (armed with everything from real weapons to farming implements) and forty archers (mostly hunters and woodsmen).

Battle
The battle took place on Flamerule 4. Two thirds of the Ffolk militia formed up along the ditch running across Freeman's Down while the remaining third stayed behind the line as a reserve. The forty Ffolk archers, the twenty mounted Sisters of Synnoria, and the sixty dwarves all remained hidden behind the top of the western hill. The Ffolk militia was ragtag, but consisted of enough lords, veterans, or respected elders that one could be stationed every twenty paces along the front line to serve as officers. Tristan's friends Daryth and Pawldo also joined the line, while the massive blacksmith Gavin led the reserves. Tristan and Robyn, alongside Tristan's moorhounds, stayed behind the front line to provide support wherever the line faltered. The famed bard Keren Donnell used his harp to inspire the troops. Meanwhile, Brigit Cu'Lyrran led the Sisters of Synnoria while Finellen led her dwarves.

When the Northmen arrived at the top of the valley, their exhausted army took its time to form up before letting out a great roar and charging the Ffolk line. Grunnarch held the Bloodriders and the fribolgs in reserve.

Amid a rain of arrows from the hill, the Northmen berserkers charged into the Ffolk line, tripping over the ditch and leaving the first wave open to the militia's first attacks. The line held surprisingly well, with Tristan and his friends rushing to close any gaps, but soon the reserves were needed. At this point, the impatient and bloodthirsty Bloodriders defied orders and charged the seemingly undefended western hill, intending to encircle the Ffolk. However, they were countered by a charge of the Sisters of Synnoria, who had the advantage of attacking downhill despite their smaller numbers. The Bloodriders' defiance also spurred the firbolg's to charge the hill, and they were likewise surprised and then routed by the dwarves.

Tristan, astride Avalon and joined by his dog Canthus, joined the Sisters of Synnoria in their fight with the Bloodriders, and clashed directly with Laric. Meanwhile, Gavin led the Ffolk in a charge that broke the Northmen's lines and sent them back to the top of the valley to regroup, ending the battle.

Aftermath

Trsitan and the Ffolk successfully stalled Grunnarch's advance and allowed the refugees to escape. That night, they retreated as the Northmen set up camp. While Tristan was very proud of his victory in the first battle he had ever led, he was admonished by his allies for failing to appreciate how minor of a victory it was and just how terrible the human cost had been. Many had died on both sides of the battle, and notable casualties included Carina, a Sister of Synnoria slain by Laric as she saved Tristan's life. Tristan also believed that his prized moorhound Canthus had been killed, but the dog survived with the intervention of Genna Moonsinger.

Tristan and his allies retreated west to Caer Corwell, where they would participate in the definitive Battle of Caer Corwell.

## Battle of Caer Corwell

The Battle of Caer Corwell was a series of clashes between the Ffolk of Corwell and Northmen raiders that marked the climax of the Darkwalker War of the . The fighting occurred around Corwell Town and the castle of Caer Corwell, in the southwest of the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles.

History
Causes
The Darkwalker War was started when the Beast Kazgaroth killed and assumed the form of King Khelgar Ironfist of Oman, and in this guise organized for a massive force of Northmen to attack and slaughter the people of Corwell. Victory would require him to destroy Corwell's capital at Caer Corwell, and so he sailed his forces to attack the town from the sea to the west while sending two other armies, led by Kings Raag Hammerstaad of Norheim and Grunnarch the Red of Norland, to raze the eastern settlements of the kingdom and approach the capital by land.

Having learned of the impending danger of Northman raiders, King Bryon Kendrick of Corwell arranged for Caer Corwell to be made ready for an attack, including summoning allies among his vassals, namely the lords of Dynnatt and Koart, as well as to have the nearby halfling settlement of Lowhill evacuated. He expected his son, Prince Tristan Kendrick, to lead Corwell Town's defenders, however the Prince departed on a personal quest the night before he was to assume this command.

Battles
Defense of the Harbor
On Flamerule 4, the fleet of "Khelgar Ironfist" arrived at Corwell Harbor. Their approach along Corwell Firth was hampered by winds summoned by a trio of druids, including Quinn Moonwane and Dierdre, until the strain of the magic caused Dierdre to expire of exhaustion. As the longships began to enter the harbor through the narrow gap in the breakwater, catapults from the town opened fire with flaming bales of straw and pitch while archers opened fire and the two remaining druids used their spells to shatter one ship and summon a fire storm to destroy another. However, Kazgoroth stood at the front of the fleet in his guise as Khelgar Ironfist, and killed both druids with his power. He then caused a wall to collapse atop King Bryon Kendrick of Corwell, who was coordinating the defense. Even so, the catapults had successfully made the Northmen turn away from the harbor, forcing them to land just outside of the breakwater to the south of Corwell Town. They did not press the attack further that day.

Fall of the Town

On Flamerule 6, Prince Tristan Kendrick took control of the defense of Corwell at his father's command, having just arrived the previous day after a minor victory over the Northmen at the Battle of Freeman's Down. Meanwhile, Lords Dynnatt and Koart, each seeking to outdo the other, had deployed to the south and were routed by the Northmen, who prodded them to retreat into the town but did not pursue. Tristan and his father both understood that the town's low walls could not hold back the attackers, and that it was not safe to allow people to remain outside the castle. Tristan thus ordered a retreat to the castle against the protests of Lord Mayor Dinsmore and the silent disapproval of Lord Koart. Following the arrival of reinforcements in the form of the Sisters of Synnoria and a company of dwarves led by Finellen, the effort to evacuate the town began. The forces of Dynnatt and Koart were deployed north along the road to the castle, but the Northmen struck them hard. Koart's forces retreated back to the walls while Dynnatt's forces were wiped out, trapping the remaining defenders and wounded within Corwell Town.

That night, following the arrival of the armies of Norheim and Norland from the east, Kazgoroth maneuvered his forces to wipe out Corwell Town: his plan was to attack from the south and east while feinting an attack in the north, thus pushing the defenders to attempt to flee north to the castle where they would be ambushed, including by his terrifying Bloodriders. The attack began just before dawn on Flamerule 7, and went according to Kazgoroth's plan until King Bryon's ward, Robyn, used the Staff of the White Well to summon a series of lighting strikes, causing the Northmen to break ranks and allowing Tristan and his forces to reach the safety of the castle. This brought Robyn's druidic power to the attention of Kazgoroth, who infiltrated the castle that night as a winged monster and attempted to kill her.

The defenders of Caer Corwell settled behind the safety of the walls while the Northmen occupied their town and began constructing mighty siege engines. Supplies were rationed to last them until the winter, and it was hoped that the seasons would break the siege even if force of arms could not.

Defense of Caer Corwell

On Flamerule 20, Kazgoroth's forces began their final assault.Dates for the events of the Darkwalker War and the Battle of Caer Corwell are given in a timeline provided in The Forgotten Realms Atlas (p. 30). However, this timeline is at odds with the novel Darkwalker on Moonshae (ch. 19), which states that the final assault on Caer Corwell occurred "eight days after the fall of Corwell Town", whereas the timeline indicates twelve days. As The Forgotten Realms Atlas is both a more recent publication and higher in this wiki's canon hierarchy, it is assumed to be correct for the purpose of this article. The Northmen began to scale the hill on which Caer Corwell sat, using ropes, ladders, and spikes in an effort to scale the walls or at least damage them with fire pots. Meanwhile, great catapults hurled cauldrons of flaming pitch against the palisade and a company of firbolgs, led by Groth, carried an enchanted battering ram up the winding road to the gate. Protected by thick leather cloaks, the firbolgs made their way to the gate and broke through the outer door while many of the defenders rushed about trying to extinguish the fires along the walls. Aiming to prevent the firbolg's from breaching the portcullis, Tristan led his personal allies (Daryth, Pawldo, and Keren Donnell) and a handful of men-at-arms to fight the firbolgs in the tight quarters of the gatehouse, succeeding only when they were joined by Finellen's dwarves.

Soon after, the Northmen successfully breached the eastern palisade, but the defenders (led by Tristan's friend Gavin) managed to hold the line with the help of Robyn's druidic magic. With an opening in the wall now made, Kazgoroth's Bloodriders enacted a ritual to grant themselves and their steeds supernatural speed, which they used to race up the hill and carve a bloody path through the defenders, killing Gavin and beginning to slaughter the Ffolk in the castle courtyard. The Sisters of Synnoria mounted a charge from the courtyard stables, drawing the Bloodriders' attention and luring them into position for Robyn to annihilate the riders with a wall of fire save for their leader, Laric. By this time, Kazgoroth (still in the guise of Khelgar Ironfist) had scaled the hill with his forces and arrived in the courtyard, where he was confronted by Tristan wielding the Sword of Cymrych Hugh. In the chaos, Laric abducted Robyn and fled the battle, intending to consume her life essence and betraying his master Kazgoroth to do so.

Meanwhile, the Pack had arrived from the north. This violent "child" of the Ffolk's Goddess consisted of thousands of wolves from across Gwynneth, all currently being led by Canthus, Tristan's own prized moorhound. The wolves tore into the Northmen's rearguard, overwhelming and slaughtering them. After King Raag of Norheim fell to the wolves, King Grunnarch of Norland decided to retreat back to his longships, abandoning the fight. As the tide turned against the Northmen, Kazgorth's anger overwhelmed him, causing him to lose control over his shape and assume his true, monstrous form. He too then fled the losing battle, following Laric's trail toward Myrloch Vale, and the remaining Northmen lost all morale and fled for their ships. As they ran, they were cut down by the Pack as well as by the pursuing Ffolk, now led by the surprise reappearance of their badly injured King Bryon (who had been strapped into his saddle to allow him to ride). Rather than join the fighting, Tristan and his companions hastily outfitted themselves for travel and raced in pursuit of Laric and Kazgoroth, hoping to save Robyn and end the threat to the kingdom.

Aftermath
The Ffolk victory at Caer Corwell marked the end of the fighting with the Northmen in the Darkwalker War, although the threat of Kazgoroth was not ended until the Beast was slain by Tristan on Eleasis 5.

The Pack, which had been summoned by the Earthmother to fight Kazgoroth, dispersed once the Northmen had been driven from Corwell Town, and was not seen again for many years.

The great deeds of Tristan and Robyn at the Battle of Caer Corwell soon spread, marking them as threats to the evil schemes of Cyndre, leader of the Council of Seven, who arranged to have them assassinated.
